records.title: Ethereum vs. Bitcoin: Major Shift Ahead for the ETH/BTC Pair?
records.summary_text:
[CW note] From the CryptoWeeklies video of 13 September 2026.

[2026-09-13_ETH/BTC]  
Video Title: Ethereum vs. Bitcoin: Major Shift Ahead for the ETH/BTC Pair?  
Video ID: wOZTE9uR2Is  
Ethereum vs. Bitcoin (ETH/BTC) | Class: CRYPTO  

Current Structure  
The pair is trading near 0.32 BTC per ETH, a sharp rise from the 0.10 BTC/ETH level seen in 2022 and the 0.03 BTC/ETH range of 2025‑2026. The 20‑week SMA is breached, and the 100‑week SMA sits at roughly 31, indicating a short‑term overextension. Composite risk scores flag a forecasted return of -5% and a risk level exceeding 60%, while social sentiment remains volatile with frequent mentions of “overvaluation” and “breakout.”  

Macro Quantitative Risk  
TWAP baselines are anchored at the 0.32 BTC/ETH level, with TWAP risk levels above 60% suggesting heightened volatility. Polynomial regression fair‑value bands have trended downward since 2022, creating a residual zone where the pair is currently overvalued relative to its long‑term mean. The gravity model places the pair at risk level one or two, implying that accumulation is only defensible if the valuation falls below the 0.27‑0.28 BTC/ETH primary stop.  

Downside & Upside Targets  
Machine‑learning forecasts project a potential reversal to the 0.026 BTC/ETH floor, with a non‑panic drawdown support around 0.03 BTC/ETH. Macro moving‑average supports at the 20‑week and 100‑week levels provide short‑term resistance, while a 200‑week S&5 anchor suggests a longer‑term bullish target near 0.40 BTC/ETH. Cycle analysis indicates that a sustained rally could push the pair back toward the 0.31 BTC/ETH high seen in April 2026, but only if the lower‑high structure persists.

records.title: Why ETH/BTC Triggered a Bleeding Zone Warning on Our Crypto Galaxy Matrix
records.summary_text:
[CW note] From the CryptoWeeklies video of 5 August 2026.

[2026-08-05_ETH/BTC]  
Video Title: Why ETH/BTC Triggered a Bleeding Zone Warning on Our Crypto Galaxy Matrix  
Video ID: MNssbw8gtjM  
ETH/BTC (ETH/BTC) | Class: CRYPTO  

Current Structure  
The ETH/BTC pair is trading at a ratio of 0.029 (ETH ≈ $1,856 against BTC at $64,000), placing ETH well above its 20‑day SMA but below both the 100‑day and 200‑day SMAs. The composite risk score sits at 66, indicating moderate opportunity cost and low mean‑reversion pressure. Social‑sentiment analysis shows a sharp spike in negative chatter, with a word‑cloud dominated by “panic,” “sell,” and “bottom.”  

Macro Quantitative Risk  
The time‑average price (TWAP) baseline for ETH relative to BTC is 0.0183, with the current valuation exceeding this by roughly 36 %, creating a premium‑discount gap. Regression‑based fair‑value bands place the pair in a “segmentation” zone, and the risk level is classified as 2 (between 10 and 20 on the scale). The model flags a forward‑output of about 6 % potential drawdown if conditions worsen.  

Downside & Upside Targets  
Machine‑learning forecasts project a major panic by January 2027, with a potential double‑bottom test in the second half of 2026. The downside support floor is estimated near 0.018 (≈ $1,100), while upside targets aim for a rally to 0.04 (≈ $2,560) if the bullish seasonality resumes. The model warns that a sustained breach of the 20‑day SMA could trigger a rapid pullback, whereas a rebound above the 100‑day SMA would signal a new bullish cycle.

Current Structure  
The pair is trading near 0.32 BTC per ETH, a sharp rise from the 0.10 BTC/ETH level seen in 2022 and the 0.03 BTC/ETH range of 2025‑2026. The 20‑week SMA is breached, and the 100‑week SMA sits at roughly 31, indicating a short‑term overextension. Composite risk scores flag a forecasted return of -5% and a risk level exceeding 60%, while social sentiment remains volatile with frequent mentions of “overvaluation” and “breakout.”  

Macro Quantitative Risk  
TWAP baselines are anchored at the 0.32 BTC/ETH level, with TWAP risk levels above 60% suggesting heightened volatility. Polynomial regression fair‑value bands have trended downward since 2022, creating a residual zone where the pair is currently overvalued relative to its long‑term mean. The gravity model places the pair at risk level one or two, implying that accumulation is only defensible if the valuation falls below the 0.27‑0.28 BTC/ETH primary stop.

Machine‑learning forecasts project a potential reversal to the 0.026 BTC/ETH floor, with a non‑panic drawdown support around 0.03 BTC/ETH. Macro moving‑average supports at the 20‑week and 100‑week levels provide short‑term resistance, while a 200‑week S&5 anchor suggests a longer‑term bullish target near 0.40 BTC/ETH. Cycle analysis indicates that a sustained rally could push the pair back toward the 0.31 BTC/ETH high seen in April 2026, but only if the lower‑high structure persists.
